tagline: A large sheltered bay metro with real commuter water-taxi precedent and a revitalized downtown waterfront.
summary: Tampa Bay is one of the largest sheltered estuaries in the US, ringed by Tampa, St Petersburg, Clearwater and (to the south) Sarasota and the Anna Maria barrier islands. The bay already runs a downtown water-taxi and the Cross-Bay Ferry pilot between St Pete and Tampa, proving latent demand for a water tier across a bay where the bridges — Howard Frankland, Gandy, Sunshine Skyway — are chronic chokepoints. A revitalized St Pete and the Water Street Tampa waterfront support both premium and commuter use, and Sarasota and Anna Maria add an affluent resort-island layer to the south.

navier_fit.pioneer_ii: Pioneer II owns the whole bay network: St Pete ↔ Tampa, Clearwater, and the Sarasota / Anna Maria corridor — all comfortably in sheltered-bay all-electric range.
navier_fit.quanta_lr: Quanta-LR is not required for the bay network; available for any future open-Gulf leg.

competitive_landscape: The Cross-Bay Ferry (slow displacement) and the Pirate Water Taxi are both demand proof and incumbents. No fast-water service exists. Bridge tolls and shallow bay sections are operational factors. HART / PSTA are the transit-authority partners; Uber is the demand platform.
seasonality: Year-round demand on the commuter/downtown side; the Nov–Apr season adds resort-island leisure demand. Hurricane season (Jun–Nov) is the main disruption; the sheltered bay stays workable in most conditions.
regulatory_note: US Coast Guard Subchapter T inspection; HART / PSTA transit coordination for any public-transit service; Florida clean-marina and manatee/no-wake zones favor zero-emission, low-wake operation.

precedents.what: San Francisco Bay Ferry / WETA network
precedents.why_it_matters: Shows a mature bay-ferry authority model Tampa Bay's geography and ferry precedent can grow into.
